items.followUp: Name the three stages of the cell cycle’s interphase.

rubric.why: G₁ and S are two of the three phases of interphase.
rubric.description: Names G₁ phase and S phase.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when both G₁ and S are named.

rubric.why: G₂ is the remaining phase of interphase.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when G₂ is named.

modelAnswer: The three phases of interphase are G₁ phase, S phase and G₂ phase.

items.followUp: Explain how transpiration helps in the upward movement of water and minerals in a plant.

rubric.why: Identifies water evaporation from the leaves as the source of the pulling force.
rubric.description: Defines transpirational pull as the pulling force produced when water evaporates from leaves during transpiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking water loss from leaves with a pulling force.

rubric.why: States the role of the pull in the upward movement of water and minerals.
rubric.description: Explains that it helps move water and dissolved minerals upward from the roots through the xylem to the leaves.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the pull helps in the upward transport of water and minerals, or that it causes the ascent of sap.

modelAnswer: Transpirational pull is the pulling force created in the xylem when water evaporates from the leaves during transpiration.
It helps draw water and dissolved minerals from the roots up through the xylem to the leaves; this upward movement is called the ascent of sap.
